title: Flow-center alignment reduced the Ob-Yenisey peak pairing excess in 31 certified years from 1980 to 2011
abstract: We tested whether year-to-year flow timing accounts for a peak association that remained after seasonal volumes were held constant. We used ArcticGRO v20261104 daily discharge at Ob-Salekhard and Yenisey-Igarka in 31 common certified years from 1980 to 2011. Each April-August hydrograph was scaled to its river mean volume. Integer translation then aligned each flow center to its river mean center while retaining relative daily shape and volume. The mean seven-day peak excess above independent year pairing fell from 1,586.91 to 272.87 cubic metres per second. The direct reduction was 1,314.04, or 82.8%, with conditional permutation p = 0.0087. A conditional paired-year bootstrap range was 123.09 to 2,331.80. Median-date alignment and alternate period groups retained positive reductions. We also found that an earlier pair study used different permutation groups in its code and text. Both rules retain the reduction, with weaker support for the coded rule. This is a diagnostic extension on overlapping data, not an independent confirmation or a causal weather test. Short coverage, regulation, fixed seasonal cuts, source error, conditional exchangeability and absent coastal routing limit inference. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate draws, a figure and independent arithmetic checks support reproduction. Source records and annual derivatives remain external.

display.caption: Equal-volume peak excess before and after flow-center alignment. Left: fixed-transformation paired-year bootstrap ranges. Right: conditional permutation reference for the reduction. Neither panel measures coastal freshwater delivery.
